meta_description: Cyber & Zero-Trust for Manufacturing & Industrial: delivery pattern, compliance frame, platforms and committed outcomes from Dataq Software.

blocks.x: What Cyber & Zero-Trust changes inside Manufacturing & Industrial: the processes we target, the controls we inherit, the platforms underneath, and the measured delta at every gate.

In Manufacturing & Industrial, cybersecurity & zero-trust covers architecture-level security programs: zero-trust network and workload design, identity modernization, threat intelligence and managed detection, cloud posture management, ai-specific security for models and agents, cyber resilience, and the compliance machinery (soc 2, iso 27001, pci dss, dora) that regulated industries must evidence. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: zero-trust architecture & implementation, threat intelligence & managed soc, identity & access modernization — delivered on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: IT/OT convergence exposure
Plant networks flatten as sensors and remote access multiply; legacy HMIs and flat topologies make ransomware and sabotage credible threats with physical consequences.
Brownfield instrumentation gap
Critical assets run uninstrumented because gut-and-replace is unthinkable; the data that twins and models need does not exist, and downtime for retrofit is unaffordable.
Quality escapes and manual inspection

Defect detection depends on sampling and eyes; escapes reach customers, and scrap/rework costs hide in the P&L. Vision systems stall in pilot because lighting, thresholds and line integration were never engineered.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

Under the hood the pattern composes 7 Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust services — Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation, Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC, Identity & Access Modernization, Cloud Security & Posture Management as the usual core — sequenced by the Dataq Method, with NIS2 (EU operators) obligations shaping design decisions from the first sprint onward.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation
Never trust, always verify: zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC
Detection that keeps pace: intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.
Identity & Access Modernization
Identity as the perimeter: workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
Cloud Security & Posture Management
Secure at the control plane: posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
OT segmentation program
IEC 62443 zones-and-conduits with monitoring and remote-access control (flat plant networks eliminated)
OT recovery playbooks
Restoration-tested backups and manual-fallback procedures for production lines (recovery time proven in drills)
Root-cause investigation time
From weeks to hours with correlated telemetry
Unplanned downtime on critical assets
Down 30-50% within a year of instrumented prediction
Defect escape rate on instrumented stations
Down sharply with vision closed loops

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: NIS2 (EU operators) and ESG reporting (CSRD/ISSB). Plant-level energy and emissions data with auditability. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

A fixed rhythm keeps progress visible from week one — here is the one we run. The first two weeks lock the baseline: your team and ours measure the current metric together and sign it. Weeks 3–8 carry the pilot on bounded scope — a single decision path, workflow, plant or portfolio — and a control owner on your side owns the evidence. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement, and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Missing a gate produces a documented decision to stop or redirect — never a silent extension.
